issues.t: Internal water pump leaks coolant into the oil
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no puddle under the car, a low-coolant or overheating warning, milky or tan sludge on the oil cap, or rough running as the engine gets damaged.
issues.why: On the 3.5L and 3.7L V6 the water pump sits inside the engine and is driven by the timing chain. When its seal wears out, coolant can leak straight into the oil instead of dripping outside, which can ruin the engine bearings.
issues.next: If coolant is disappearing, stop driving and have a cooling system pressure test and oil check done right away. Catching it before coolant mixes with the oil is the difference between a pump job and a new engine.

issues.t: AWD power transfer unit leaks and overheats
issues.sym: A burning gear-oil smell after driving, drips near the passenger-side front axle, or a groaning noise and shudder on AWD models. In bad cases the AWD unit fails completely.
issues.why: The power transfer unit that sends power to the rear wheels runs hot next to the exhaust and holds very little fluid. Its seals leak and the oil cooks, wearing out the gears.
issues.next: Have any leak near the right front axle checked to see whether it is transmission or transfer unit oil. Changing the transfer unit fluid early and fixing seal leaks can save the unit.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Hard or late shifts, the engine revving between gears, slipping, fluid leaks, or the SUV getting stuck in one gear.
issues.why: Owners of early MKX models report six-speed automatic wear and failures, often around 70,000 to 110,000 miles, sometimes after leaks lowered the fluid level.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and look for leaks. If shifts are slipping, get a transmission diagnosis soon; driving on it usually turns a repair into a rebuild.

issues.t: Takata passenger airbag inflator can rupture (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The danger shows up only in a crash, when the passenger airbag can burst and throw metal pieces.
issues.why: The Takata inflator propellant breaks down over years of heat and humidity and can explode with too much force. Several recalls cover the original and replacement inflators, and some carry a do-not-drive warning.
issues.next: Check your VIN on nhtsa.gov/recalls today. If the recall is open, do not drive the vehicle; ask a Lincoln dealer for a free repair and a tow if needed.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can explode (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms before a crash. In a crash, the driver airbag inflator can rupture and send fragments into the cabin.
issues.why: The driver-side inflator propellant can degrade with humidity and heat, the same problem behind the passenger inflator recalls.
issues.next: Look up your VIN for recall 21V-158 and get the free replacement as soon as possible.

issues.t: Fuel tank seam can rust and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gasoline smell around the car, or wet spots and drips under the rear seat area.
issues.why: Road salt can corrode the welded seam on the fuel tank until fuel seeps out, a fire risk. Separate recalls cover 2007-2008 and 2009-2010 models.
issues.next: If you smell fuel, park outside away from buildings and have the tank inspected. Check your VIN for recalls 14V-682 and 15V-712.

issues.t: Brake booster can fail (extended warranty)
issues.sym: A brake pedal that goes soft or sinks toward the floor, a hard pedal that needs extra force, a hissing sound when pressing the brakes, or longer stops.
issues.why: The vacuum brake booster that multiplies pedal force can fail internally. Ford extended the warranty on the booster for certain 2010-2014 Edge and MKX models.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Get the brakes checked right away if the pedal feels different. Ask a Lincoln dealer whether your VIN is covered by the extended booster warranty (program 13N02).

issues.t: Door ajar light stays on and drains the battery
issues.sym: The door ajar warning stays lit with all doors shut, interior lights stay on or flicker, the doors may not lock, and the battery can be dead in the morning.
issues.why: The switch inside a door latch wears and tells the car a door is open. Ford issued several bulletins for this on 2011-2013 Edge and MKX models.
issues.next: Note which door the dash shows as open and have that latch replaced. Ask the dealer about Ford bulletin TSB 18-2013.

issues.t: Power steering fluid leak at the pressure hose
issues.sym: Red or amber fluid dripping near the front of the engine, a whining pump, or steering that feels heavier at low speed. A pump squeal at full steering lock is also reported on 2011-2013 models.
issues.why: The fitting where the high-pressure hose attaches to the steering rack can leak. Low fluid then makes the pump noisy and can wear it out.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level and look for wet spots on the hose. Replacing the hose or seals early protects the pump.

issues.t: Front halfshaft can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk, then a sudden loss of drive power, or the SUV rolling in Park if the parking brake is not set.
issues.why: The clip that holds the front axle shaft into the transmission may not have been installed correctly, so the shaft can slip out.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 14V-393. Always set the parking brake when parked until the free repair is done.

issues.t: "Not in Park" warning and roll-away risk
issues.sym: The dash says the transmission is not in Park after you shift to Park, and the SUV may creep or roll, especially on a slope.
issues.why: The shifter or its Park sensing switch does not fully register the Park position. Owners report replacing the shifter assembly.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake, and have the shifter checked. Do not leave the vehicle running and unattended while this warning shows.

issues.t: Engine stalls or loses power while driving
issues.sym: The engine shuts off or loses throttle while moving, often at low speed, sometimes with a wrench light or check engine light. It usually restarts.
issues.why: Owners report a range of fixes, most often a replaced electronic throttle body; a faulty evaporative purge valve and loose wiring were found in other cases.
issues.next: Pull over safely if it happens and have the codes read soon, even if it restarts. Ask the dealer about throttle body bulletins and owner letters for your VIN.

issues.t: Front brake hoses can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid on the inside of a front wheel, or a brake warning light.
issues.why: The front brake hoses can wear and burst early, letting fluid escape and making stops longer.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for recall 20V-469. If the pedal feels soft, do not drive until the brakes are inspected.

issues.t: Rear brake hose can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: A softer brake pedal, fluid near a rear wheel, or a brake warning light.
issues.why: A rear brake hose can crack and leak fluid as the suspension moves, reducing braking.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. Check your VIN for recall 25V-544 and get the free hose replacement.

issues.t: Seat frame can damage airbag wiring (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light comes on, or a seat side airbag may not work. In rare cases an airbag could go off unexpectedly.
issues.why: On seats with the tilt feature, the seat frame can rub through the wiring for the seat airbag and seat belt system.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-414. Have the airbag light diagnosed promptly.

issues.t: Battery cable can short against shifter bracket (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell, electrical problems, or in the worst case smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: A battery cable harness can rub against a bracket on the transmission shifter until it shorts, a fire risk.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 19V-809. If you smell burning wiring, stop and turn the vehicle off.

issues.t: Door striker bolts may be too short (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. In a crash a door could open.
issues.why: Some doors were built with striker bolts that are too short to hold the latch firmly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-612 and have the bolts replaced for free.

issues.t: Harsh or jerky shifts from the 8-speed automatic
issues.sym: Clunks when shifting into Drive or Reverse, bumpy or harsh shifts at low speed, shudder under acceleration, or what feels like slipping between gears.
issues.why: Ford bulletin TSB 19-2103 says early 2019 Nautilus and Edge models with the 8-speed automatic can shift harshly because of the transmission computer settings. Some vehicles also needed valve body or transmission work.
issues.next: Ask a Lincoln dealer to check for software updates. If shifts stay harsh after the update, keep records of every visit while it is under warranty.

issues.t: Instrument cluster may stay blank (recall)
issues.sym: The gauge cluster stays dark when you start the car, so no speed, warnings or gear are shown.
issues.why: Instrument cluster software can fail to start up. The first fix (19V-076) did not fully solve it, so a second recall (26V-372) was issued.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN for both recalls and have the update done even if the first one was completed.

issues.t: Transmission fluid leak from start-stop accumulator (recall)
issues.sym: Red fluid drips under the car, rough shifting, or loss of drive power.
issues.why: The bolts holding the start-stop accumulator to the transmission can be loose or missing, letting fluid leak out.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 20V-550. If you see transmission fluid leaking, do not keep driving.

issues.t: Backup camera image blank or stuck on (recalls)
issues.sym: The rear camera shows a blank or distorted picture in Reverse, or the image stays on after you shift out of Reverse.
issues.why: A loose camera connection (20V-575) or a software error (25V-442) can disrupt the camera feed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls and get the free fix.

issues.t: 2.7L ticking or tapping on cold start
issues.sym: A tick or tap from the engine for a short time after starting, mainly after the car has sat for six hours or more.
issues.why: Ford bulletin TSB 23-2049, later updated by TSB 23-2356, covers this cold-start noise on 2019-2023 Edge and Nautilus models with the 2.7L engine.
issues.next: Ask a Lincoln dealer to check it against those bulletins, especially while the powertrain warranty is in effect.

issues.t: AWD chatter or shudder in tight turns
issues.sym: A chatter, shudder or binding feeling from the rear in slow, tight turns such as parking lots.
issues.why: Ford service messages point to worn or contaminated fluid in the rear drive unit clutch.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the rear drive unit and fluid; a fluid change or a clutch service kit is often the fix.

issues.t: AWD rear drive unit low on oil can seize (recall)
issues.sym: A whine or grinding from the rear, then possibly a rear axle that locks up.
issues.why: Some rear drive units left the factory without enough oil, which can wear them out and seize the axle.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-011 and have the rear drive unit inspected and refilled.

issues.t: Backup camera image delayed, frozen or blank (recall)
issues.sym: The rear camera picture is slow to appear, freezes, or is missing when you shift into Reverse.
issues.why: A software error in the camera system can delay or stop the image.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-315 and get the free software update.

issues.t: Intake valves can break in the 2.7L engine (recall)
issues.sym: Engine misfire, rough running, loud knocking, or a sudden loss of power while driving.
issues.why: Some 2.7L engines have intake valves that can break, which can destroy the engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-635. If the engine starts running rough or knocking, pull over and have it towed.

issues.t: Upper engine knock from the left cylinder head
issues.sym: A thump or knock from the top of the engine on the driver side.
issues.why: Ford service message SSM 51665 covers this noise on 2021-2023 vehicles with the 2.7L engine.
issues.next: Have a Lincoln dealer inspect it while the vehicle is under warranty.

issues.t: Rear shocks may be built wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Knocking from the rear suspension, poor ride control, or a brake warning light.
issues.why: Some rear shocks may have been built incorrectly and can damage the brake hose and nearby parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-439 and have the shocks inspected.

issues.t: Power windows may not reverse on an obstruction (recalls)
issues.sym: A window keeps closing on a hand or object instead of backing off, especially when using the close-all-windows feature.
issues.why: Window control software does not reverse correctly or far enough. The first fixes did not fully work, so follow-up recalls were issued.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 24V-597, 24V-953, 25V-237 and 25V-518, and keep hands clear when closing windows remotely.

issues.t: Engine block heater can overheat when plugged in (recall)
issues.sym: A hot or burning smell from the front of the car when the block heater is plugged in.
issues.why: The engine block heater can overheat while in use, a fire risk.
issues.next: Do not plug in the block heater until recall 25V-343 is done.

issues.t: Camera and driver-assist features drop out (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera goes blank and driver-assist features turn off, often with warning messages.
issues.why: The image processing module can reset while driving.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-165 and get the free update.

issues.t: Center screens go blank or reboot (recall)
issues.sym: The main displays go black or restart while driving.
issues.why: A software bug in the multimedia system can reboot the screens.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-337 and get the software update.

issues.t: EGR valve can fail and cut engine power (recall)
issues.sym: A sudden loss of power, check engine light, or the engine going into a reduced-power mode.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation valve can fail, which may cause a sudden loss of drive power.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-122 and get the free valve replacement.

issues.t: Headlights or other lights can go out (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights or other exterior lights stop working, often with a lighting warning message.
issues.why: The LED driver module that powers the lights can burn out.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 25V-519 and avoid night driving if a headlight is out.
